en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Fourth Chapter
The Discourse on Whether a Householder Can Be an Arahant. "Can a householder be an arahant?
"Yes, he can."
Is there a fetter of household life for an arahant?
One should not say so...
Is it not the case that there is no fetter of household life for an arahant?
“Yes.
“If there is no householder-fetter for an Arahant, then indeed it should not be said:
‘An Arahant is a householder.’”
“Is it possible for a householder to be an Arahant?”—
“Yes.”—
“But has the fetter of household life not been abandoned by the Arahant, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and made subject to non-arising in the future?”
“Yes.

“If it is true that for an Arahant the fetter of being a householder has been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like the stump of a palm tree, rendered non-existent, and is subject to non-arising in the future,
then surely you should not say, ‘An Arahant is a householder.’”
Is it possible for a householder to be an arahant? Yes.
Is there any householder who, without abandoning the fetters of household life, makes an end of suffering in this very life? No.
There is none.
If there is no householder who, without having abandoned the fetter of household life, makes an end of suffering in this very life, then indeed it should not be said:
"A householder is an Arahant."
“Is it the case that a householder can be an arahant? “Yes.
“But did not the wanderer Vacchagotta say this to the Blessed One:”
“Is there, Master Gotama, any householder who, without abandoning the fetter of household life, makes an end of suffering at the breaking up of the body?
“There is no such person, Vaccha, any householder who, without abandoning the fetter of household life, makes an end of suffering at the breaking up of the body.
“Is this indeed a sutta?”
“Yes,
[it would follow]. Therefore, it should not be said that “a householder is an Arahant.”
Is it possible for a householder to be an arahant? Yes.
[If so,] could an arahant engage in sexual intercourse, produce sexual desire, or dwell in a bed crowded with children?
One might enjoy Kāsī sandalwood; one might wear garlands, perfumes, and ointments; one might accept gold and silver; one might accept goats and sheep;
one might accept chickens and pigs; one might accept elephants, cows, horses, and mares;
one might accept partridges, quails, peacocks, and pigeons; one might wear a head-ornament of variegated silk and hair; and [one might wear] white...
"Would he wear garments with long fringes and remain a householder for as long as life lasts?
"Certainly not. ... [as before] ...
It should not be said.
“Is one who is a householder an Arahant?”—
“Yes.”—
“But did not the clansman Yasa, the householder Uttiya, and the young brahmin Setu attain Arahantship while still bearing the marks of a householder?”
“Yes.
“If the clansman Yasa, the householder Uttiya, and the youth Setu attained arahantship while still bearing the marks of a householder, then indeed it must be said:
‘A householder can be an arahant.’”
The discussion on whether a householder can be an arahant is finished.
